content.title: About
content.content: The chicken fillet sandwich is a popular lunch option in school cafeterias. It consists of tender boiled or baked chicken fillet, a slice of cheese, lettuce, and a sauce placed between two pieces of whole‑grain bread. A nutritious and convenient meal suitable for school‑age children.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken fillet is one of the leanest meat options, low in fat.
School cafeterias often use whole‑grain bread, which provides more fiber than white bread.
Sandwiches are easy to portion and wrap in paper packets for service.
A single sandwich provides about 15–20 g of protein, covering a significant part of a child's daily requirement.
The combination of chicken and vegetables enhances the absorption of B‑vitamins.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken fillet supplies high‑quality protein essential for growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with red meat, chicken fillet contains less saturated fat, supporting heart health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Fiber from whole‑grain bread
items.content: Whole‑grain bread adds dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The sandwich provides iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of children may be allergic to poultry and need an alternative.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Sauces and cheese can increase salt levels; moderation is recommended.

items.title: Temperature control
items.content: Chicken must be fully cooked and kept at proper temperatures to prevent foodborne illness.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Whole‑grain bread contains gluten, which may be an issue for children with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich can be served warm or at room temperature. It pairs well with fresh vegetables (tomato, cucumber) or a light yogurt sauce. For younger children, cutting it into halves makes it easier to handle.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared sandwich should be kept in the refrigerator for no more than 4 hours at +4 °C. For longer storage, keep the components (fillet, bread, vegetables) separate in airtight containers.
